This study investigates the linear, adiabastopic stability of slowly rotating stellar layers subject to self-gravitating magnetized perturbations, where the transverse vector potential is either constant or linearly varying. We establish that the presence of mutually supportive crescent-shaped ($x$) and circular ($z$) field components can trigger the classic Cylindrical Magnetorotational Instability (MRI), causing complete chaos. Conversely, in cases of strong field alignment, a stabilizing Cylindrical MRI-like effect, or what we call the "reverse" MRI, occurs. Notably, stellar gravity fields act as a double-edged sword: for specific magnetic field configurations, they are capable of simultaneously destabilize these regions. We also identify a phenomenon resembling the "reverse" MRI, where gravity acts to suppress the standard MHD turbulence. This research contributes new insights into how magnetized stellar layers evolve over time.

The analogy linking renormalization group equations to fluid dynamics serves as a vivid illustration of the inherent irreversibility in RG trajectories, manifest through the c-function's monotonic decrease. In this work, we derive the specific fluid dual for the RG flows governing conformal matter on de Sitter space across all dimensions, utilizing a Poincar\'e patch coordinate system. By employing infalling coordinates in anti-de Sitter space, we demonstrate that the dynamics of matter near the AdS boundary align precisely with a two-dimensional reduced fluid dual, resulting in an RG-invariant c-function value equal to this reduced dimension. Furthermore, we show that the "analogous" fluid dual's initial conditions are directly determined by the central charges appearing in the c-theorem coefficients of the underlying theory.

Discovering the lyrics and soundtracks for a specific song can be more efficiently achieved through a dedicated service than by relying on general web search methods. If user requirements differ from those of lyric streaming platforms, leveraging specialized service becomes an optimal solution. This paper introduces a mechanism for integrating such a service into Microsoft Word, demonstrating how it can facilitate easier access to both audio and textual content. The approach described here represents a functional prototype. Testing results confirm that this mechanism successfully locates streaming links for both lyrics and corresponding music.

In the context of topological groupoids, an extension by a group that is multiplicatively topologically non-trivial functions as the categorical analogue of a non-trivial multiplicative topological covering space structure, serving as the primary motivation for investigating topological stacky versions and their associated gerbes. This inquiry proves particularly compelling when examining extensions of complex algebraic groupoids that are generically injective, where the image constitutes a generic covering group. In this scenario, the resulting topological gerbe is trivial both algebraically along the complex structure and generally across any given field of definition. As a secondary outcome, we provide a topological stacky formulation for a result by Roseman regarding groupoid extensions that are generically injective.

The conversion of molecular cloud cores into massive stars is governed by core fragmentation, a process that remains difficult to study due to the scarcity of high-resolution data. This study utilizes the ASTROSUB-COLLS project to run adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) hydrodynamic simulations of turbulent, self-gravitating cores, tracking the evolution of core mass and the internal clump population throughout the collapse. The results indicate a robust correlation between a core's final mass and its initial clump abundance; specifically, cores with high initial clump counts undergo more rapid mass growth and reach stellar masses sooner than those that are clump-poor. Furthermore, the model demonstrates that core mass growth is driven primarily by the accretion of material onto these internal clumps. This mechanism offers a compelling explanation for the observed tendency of the most massive stars to reside in extensive stellar clusters.

This study introduces a novel 3D LiDAR benchmark tailored for scene understanding, integrating six diverse datasets. Existing point cloud segmentation and classification models typically treat each sample point in isolation, disregarding valuable contextual clues offered by adjacent points. Such neighboring context is acknowledged as essential for enhancing the performance of 3D point network architectures. To encourage the development of advanced point cloud classifiers that effectively capture such information, we introduce a simple yet powerful baseline model. This baseline achieves state-of-the-art results on two evaluated tasks: KITTI single-object classification and SUNRGB-D part-level scene segmentation. Our method leverages a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) layer to construct a sparse Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) directly from point features to build a graph structure. We determine the optimal connectivity by identifying the shortest path on a point-wise Voronoi diagram, resulting in a unique graph for every point cloud. Crucally, this approach requires no manual design regarding graph topology. Experiments indicate that this learned graph structure surpasses standard $\kappa$ neighbors methods, using significantly fewer $\kappa$ values. We also show that increasing $\kappa$ only marginally improves standard GC baselines, suggesting our data-driven topology outperforms simple spatial context aggregation.

This work investigates the maintenance of positive definiteness within zonal functions $f$ under classical operations of differentiation and integration. We establish conditions ensuring that such functions remain positively definite following differentiation with respect to the radius of the support of $f$, as well as integration over the unit circle while keeping this support constant. Additionally, we examine related scenarios, including differentiation and integration of functions that are radial on a cone with the vertex at the origin, as well as those defined as Macbeath zonal functions.

Recent observations from the TARA collaboration have established a statistically significant correlation between the arrival directions of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) and high-energy neutrinos. Building on this, our work investigates whether neutrinos can serve as reliable indicators for specific UHECR events. We find that while the neutrino flux is elevated in the directions of the highest-energy UHECRs, the statistical excess is modest, with a neutrino event rate roughly 3 to 4 times that predicted by background models. Furthermore, the neutrino statistics indicate a lack of robust directionality, as the clustering of the two highest-energy UHECR signals is not statistically independent of the measured neutrinos. Consequently, although these results do not invalidate the TANA findings, they demonstrate that current neutrino detectors cannot yet pinpoint the exact origins of the most extreme UHECRs.

This study presents a comprehensive analysis of the roughness factor ($\varepsilon$) in liquid foams, which is a critical yet historically elusive parameter governing the flow of foam through porous media. We demonstrate that roughness is dominated by the largest bubbles, with a magnitude of $\varepsilon \approx d_{\text{max}}/3$, where $d_{\text{max}}$ denotes the scale of Plateau borders. By integrating this finding with the two-fluid model, we achieve a holistic description of porous media foam flow, accurately predicting both roughness effects and the transition between viscous regimes. Furthermore, we offer a method to kinetically alter $d_{\text{max}}$ via shear thinning, enabling roughness tuning across a span exceeding an order of magnitude via phase transitions in surfactant films. These results hold significant promise for optimizing industrial applications, such as enhanced oil recovery.

Ensemble methods are well-recognized for their efficacy in boosting the accuracy of machine-learning models, yet research into applying such techniques to Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) has largely remained underdeveloped. This study introduces ENA-CNNEnsembles, a technique that integrates multiple diverse base-CNNs into a cohesive ensemble. These base models are generated by employing various architectural designs, training on different subsets of data, or both. Among the key findings is the conclusion that creating ensemble members through training data diversity alone yields significant accuracy improvements compared to using data diversity in combination with architectural diversity. Furthermore, the research highlights that data-subset diversity serves as a more reliable indicator of accuracy gains than architectural diversity, suggesting that these factors do not contribute equally to ensemble performance.

This paper examines the classic problem of rotating Rayleigh instability within a Hele-Shaw cell, where a growing droplet of immiscible fluid faces tension against a surrounding, continuous phase. Tension acts as a selection mechanism for specific drop shapes, creating a competition between tension and centrifugal forces that determines whether the droplet adopts a compact droplet shape, an elongated ellipsoid form, or a membrane state. By analyzing the energy balance between surface tension and pressure differences (due to tension) across various states, we map out the growth rates associated with each configuration. Our analysis reveals that the membrane state consistently exhibits a growth rate superior to both the droplet and ellipsoid states, although the transition times between states can modify these theoretical predictions in practical scenarios. Additionally, we explore the scenario in which the outer phase is unbounded, allowing the displaced fluid to circulate back to its initial position; under these specific conditions, the rotationally Rayleigh instability is suppressed regardless of tension levels. Finally, the study presents a theoretical framework applicable to predicting similar behaviors in other systems involving competing length scales.

This paper establishes a unified framework for defining and computing infinitesimal internal microwork performed by a single system during a nonequilibrium process. We begin by formulating a general definition of this microwork applicable to any stochastic process, regardless of whether the system is in equilibrium. For states within a Markovian context, we demonstrate that this approach yields consistent results with prior theories regarding nonequilibrium states. Furthermore, we connect this concept of internal microwork to the established theory of stochastic thermodynamics. Specifically, we show that the standard formula for stochastic heating—previously formulated in terms of path irreversibility—can be reinterpreted as instantaneous, state-based internal microwork. Finally, we introduce a new formulation of the Gibbs relation applicable to both equilibrium and nonequilibrium states. This connects the performed microwork to fluctuations in internal energy and defines a specific measure of irreversibility for the underlying stochastic process.

Peers can either diminish or enhance individual curiosity; however, the mechanisms and circumstances governing these social influences on curiosity remain largely unexamined. This study utilizes a 2×2 between-subjects survey experiment with 1,500 U.S. participants to investigate how the quantity of peers displaying curious behavior and the nature of their curiosity (toward related or unrelated topics) influence subject selection on a trivia task. The findings indicate that exposure to multiple curious individuals raises one's own level of curiosity, with this effect strengthening when the specific trivia topic shared by peers is also unrelated to the task. Furthermore, this paper advances current trivia experiment methodologies by integrating eye-tracking technology. Eye-tracking analysis reveals a distinct pattern of exploratory behavior consistent with heightened curiosity. These results offer crucial insights for understanding curiosity development and inform strategic applications in domains such as trivia-based competitions, trivia-informed decision-making, and educational settings.

We introduce independent graph Matérn Gaussian processes, a flexible class of non-stationary processes suitable for both stationary and transient modeling. These processes retain conjugate characteristics that simplify inference under uncertain conditions. By parameterizing the time-varying covariance function with just two parameters, their flexibility is further constrained, facilitating data-driven selection of the self-exciting/self-inhibiting behavior (representing feedback loops) and the length of duration or range of influence. Their modular construction allows for the integration of various excitation and inhibition mechanisms, promoting interpretability regarding the underlying system dynamics. Techniques such as variational approximation make training feasible in mini-batch settings and support methods beyond standard conjugacy. Combined with recent visual tools for process interpretation, this new framework offers a robust approach to uncovering and modeling the dynamical structures hidden within diverse datasets.

In cities, the integration of ridesourcing fleets enables passive traffic sensing, which aids in addressing critical issues like intelligent transportation and smart mobility. This study addresses the optimization of such ridesourcing sensing capabilities by leveraging detailed GPS data from over 1,200 Uber trips in Phoenix, USA, to map traffic network sensitivity. GPS records allow for the identification of sensitive links—road segments where ridesourcing activity significantly influences traffic monitoring reliability. Analysis reveals that sensitivity is not distributed evenly; it clusters in specific regions and varies throughout the day and week based on time of day, week, and external factors such as weather. Furthermore, the research investigates how ridesourcing sensing efficacy changes with different levels of adoption. Counterintuitively, sensing robustness and coverage improve more rapidly in less dense networks as ridesourcing expands, rather than in highly saturated environments. Finally, the paper evaluates whether pricing strategies, such as surge pricing, impact sensing reliability by altering trip frequencies and volumes across the road network.

Taychi-Schrodinger-Schrieffer (tss) effect, originally described in the context of superconducting systems, can now be achieved in the optical domain through a hybrid optomechanical setup. The presence of the tss effect in this arrangement is indicated when the phase of the optomechanical oscillation aligns with either constructive or destructive interference, depending on the beam splitter's transmission coefficient. Furthermore, the described system allows for the remote synchronization of mechanical oscillators via the tss mechanism and offers a method to halt optomechanical energy transfer between rings by adjusting the beam splitter's transmission coefficient.

The Tsallis distribution is widely recognized as a universal model for describing systems with long-tailed distributions, including social data. This document outlines a straightforward approach to deriving the Tsallis distribution by applying a least squares method to fit a Pareto tail to the system's mid-range, followed by a gradual transition to a Gaussian distribution. Furthermore, we propose a novel, simplified method to estimate the corresponding parameters using a direct formula. Through a test applied to income and population distributions across various countries, the results demonstrate a close alignment between this new approach and the traditional standard.

We investigate gravitational perturbations within a context where a mass term is included, analyzing its implications for the degree of freedom structure in linearized gravity. Furthermore, we explore how this spurious mode influences the scattering of gravitinos in the presence of such mass terms.

Quantum systems governed by geometric dynamics are classified into four categories based on whether their dynamics are holonomic or tachonomic: symmetric spaces, Kähler manifolds, contact contact manifolds, and almost complex structures. For each class, we derive the corresponding family of Hamiltonian dynamics and demonstrate their equivalence to both real and complex dynamical systems. The concept of negative temperature is re-examined using the standard two-level model. In this approach, negative energy is assigned to the higher state to resolve conventional inconsistencies, such as placing it above infinite energy. This framework naturally extends the Carnot cycle analysis to include negative temperatures and allows for the demonstration of efficient negative-to-conversion-of-positive work. Although deep neural networks have demonstrated remarkable success in classifying and grading colorectal adenomas from chromoendoscopy images, existing approaches often rely on extensive data augmentation and are prone to overfitting due to the limited diversity of available chromoendoscopy datasets. To address these challenges, we introduce a new dataset comprising 1,000 chromoendoscopy images enhanced with virtual narrow-band imaging, accompanied by corresponding push images and high-quality histology slides. Utilizing this dataset, we developed a deep neural network-based decision support system designed to aid endoscopists in identifying and categorizing adenomas during chromoendoscopy procedures. This model was trained using image pairs that synchronized chromoendoscopy visuals with definitive histology references. Furthermore, we integrated a transfer learning strategy to narrow-band image features extracted from virtual narrow-band imageries associated with both adenomatous and non-adenomatous push images as input for chromoendoscopy analysis. Evaluation against expert annotations from two endoscopists reveals high diagnostic accuracy across all tasks: adenoma detection achieved a F1-score of 0.918, classification reached 0.888, and grading performance reached 0.853.

This work presents a novel, straightforward, and effective technique for resolving high-frequency acoustic scattering challenges involving sound-soft obstacles with arbitrary geometries. The approach utilizes standard finite element methods to extend the concept of the Hodge decomposition coefficient method, which relies on constructing an artificial boundary that mimics an impenetrable obstacle. While the original Hodge coefficient artificial obstacle method demonstrated $O(h)$ convergence for the finite element mesh size $h$ in problems with smooth obstacles, this research introduces a simplified formulation that enhances both implementation ease and computational efficiency. Notably, the new method sustains this $O(h)$ convergence even for obstacles with non-smooth geometries. Furthermore, the study establishes that the resulting linear system preserves a symmetric indefinite structure, allowing for the development of a specialized multigrid solver tailored to these characteristics. Tests using both smooth and non-smooth obstacles confirm the approach's accuracy and accuracy.

This research analyzes the water content of ordinary chondrite finds from Antarctica using stable and elemental isotopes of hydrogen, focusing on samples with low alteration levels. By comparing their H-D ratios and osmium isotopic ratios to findings from recent falls like Benenitra and Chelyabinsk, the study identifies that the bulk of H in these Antarctic meteorites originates from terrestrial contamination. In contrast, the H content in the organic carbon fractions of two specific groups—Murchison-like and Ivuna-like—derives extraterrestrial sources, with the Murchison-like fractionation occurring in two distinct components. The research further demonstrates that the two ordinary chondrite groups exhibit different histories of aqueous alteration and possess unique origins, despite both deriving material from the early solar nebula's carbonaceous chondrite parent bodies.

We offer a fresh approach to understanding integrable XXZ chains with multiple spin degrees of freedom by examining the scalar products and associated form factors within the framework of the algebraic Bethe ansatz. For specific cases involving two- and three-particle states, we explicitly construct and analyze these objects. Furthermore, we explore the relationship between XXZ chains and supersymmetric quantum mechanics, demonstrating that for limited particle counts, the forms factor and constructible matrix elements can be derived directly from supersymmetric partner potentials generated via the algebraic Bethe ansatz.

Although existing research on speech translation has largely focused on scenarios with abundant training data, there is a lack of investigations into these tasks in few-shot settings. Drawing an analogy between language and speech, this study posits that bilingual proficiency can similarly be acquired in few-shot environments through the integration of multimodal data and advanced language representations. Consequently, this work introduces several methods to enable zero- and few-shot learning for speech translation, utilizing speech and text embeddings to facilitate these processes. Performance is evaluated on the open-access, bilingual Corpus of Conversational Speech (BCT) dataset. Results indicate a significant improvement over strong baselines, with a notable 6.5 dB increase in Comparable Weighted Edit Distance (CWED) for the zero-shot approach; furthermore, the proposed few-shot method achieves a competitive CWED of 3.16 dB, surpassing the baseline by 1.5 dB.

Describing the scattering of electromagnetic radiation using multipole expansions is considered a highly effective approach for various applications, including aerosol and cloud microphysical studies. While the traditional choice is the vector spherical wave multipoles, these exhibit 2cosθ angular dependence, which prevents them from representing localized energy. Although cylindrical multipoles offer better confinement, they are less suited for plane wave scattering due to their lack of rotational symmetry. Consequently, this study evaluates a range of alternative multipoles, including Gaussian, Gabor, Bessel, and ring multipoles, to determine their relative merits. Results indicate that ring multipoles are the most efficient, requiring fewer terms for convergence with sphere size compared to others; furthermore, the use of only a few ring multipoles provides a robust method for deriving optical extinctions and backscatter coefficients.

This paper demonstrates that the Schur elements arising in the restricted Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt (PBW) basis for the affine Heisenberg-Vergne (Vergne) bracket are transformed into shifted Schur polynomials via the Harish-Chandra PWB map. These findings provide a fresh perspective on the recently established restricted PBW basis by Liu and Vergne, offering a refined Harish-Chandra PWB basis that places the central generators of the affine Borel subalgebra in normal form. Consequently, the leading terms of the Schur basis are expressed as monomials within this new Harish-Chandra PWB basis, implying that their $h$-eigenvalues are precisely these transformed Schur elements. As a direct outcome, the central charges associated with the top-degree Schur basis elements within the Schur-Weyl module context are identified as shifted Schur polynomial values.

We investigate a Left-Right Symmetric (LRS) seesaw framework incorporating minimal dark sector to address the issue of vacuum instability within the observed sector. The implementation of $D$-parity symmetry, which links the dark sector to the visible, ensures the stability of the vacuum and guarantees the consistency of the principle of dark parity. Within this setup, the mechanism for suppressing neutrino masses and the formation of the dark sector occur concurrently. The resulting implications for particle physics and cosmology are examined. Specifically, the model can account for the small observed values of neutrino mass eigenvalues while facilitating the generation of the substantial dark matter density seen in the universe. Additionally, the model predicts specific signatures in electroweak precision observables and lepton flavor violation processes. Notably, it predicts a new heavy neutrino eigenstate accessible via rare muon decays, such as $\mu \rightarrow e \gamma$ and $\mu \rightarrow 3e$.

We construct an effective low-energy Hamiltonian for a wide range of transition metal oxides, incorporating the spin-orbit coupling (SOC) of the central ion alongside relevant interactions and crystal field effects. The unitary transformation method is employed to derive simplified models applicable to various valence states, coordination geometries, and strengths of SOC relative to interaction strengths and crystal field splitting. These model Hamiltonians facilitate the investigation of magnetic states and their stability within insulating transition metal oxides. Our analysis reveals that interaction effects and SOC compete to establish either ferromagnetic or antiferromagnetic insulating orders, a phenomenon analogous to the itinerant spin-orbit coupling Mott insulator found in 5d elements with long bonds. Furthermore, our model reveals the existence of competing, long-range-ordered coexisting states in 3d compounds featuring strong SOC.

This work investigates the connection between toric complete intersection spaces and their smooth divisors via the concept of relative $I$-functions. For a single smooth divisor situated within a toric complete intersection, we present and demonstrate a formula expressing the $I$-function of the toric complete intersection in terms of those of the divisor. The formula is subsequently extended to cover scenarios involving multiple smooth divisors, thereby establishing explicit interrelations among the relative $I$-functions of a toric complete intersection and its associated divisors.

Diffusion models have emerged as state-of-the-generation for medical imaging, yet their propensity for latent code drift creates a barrier to effective generation and manipulation within the encoded space. We demonstrate that conditional diffusion models admit a low-dimensional latent representation where specific conditions map to distinct regions, allowing for navigation via discrete movements. By converting this discrete flow into a continuous one, we introduce Diffusion Model Accelerated by Latent code Extrapolation (DOLLEX), a technique for generating robust mappings between latent space conditions and image content. Beyond facilitating controlled generation of disease imagery, we show that adapting pre-trained diffusion conditions enables high-performing semantic segmentation and medical diagnosis tasks. These methods are available at https://github.com/zhenghanma/DOLLEX.

Multidimensional (MD) visualization empowers analysts to explore and comprehend data by presenting results intuitively. To improve the design of such visual interfaces, experts are often needed to interpret visual patterns. This human factor can be costly and slows down analysis. To address this, we propose "Micro-Expertise," a visualization technique that integrates AI-driven insights into user-friendly views to support working memory. Specifically, we introduce "ViDaExpert," a large language model (LLM) expert that identifies and visualizes significant data patterns using Micro-Expertise. Implemented as a chat-widget on existing MD visual tools, ViDaExpert detects relevant filters, facets, or chart types based on user views or natural language queries. It highlights key filter values to distinguish groups via color coding and suggests specific visual encodings for distinct characteristics, automatically applying the optimal view. In a study with 18 participants comparing fact-answering tasks against baseline methods, participants achieved significantly higher accuracy when using ViDaExpert, demonstrating the technique's effectiveness in enhancing real-world accuracy.

This work proposes a novel approach to approximating smooth scalar fields on unstructured 2D triangular grids by employing piecewise-defined, high-order monomial polynomials in barycentric coordinates. The method capitalizes on the property of $n$-th order monomials in barycentric coordinates to maintain exactly $O(h^{n+2})$ approximation accuracy, where $h$ signifies the mesh element's linear dimension, thereby outperforming standard approaches that utilize triangular element vertices in isolation or with periodic cloud extensions. The described technique is evaluated as a computationally efficient and straightforward means to elevate the formal order of accuracy on grids that are otherwise too irregular to support high-order finite volume or spectral element methods. The enhancement in performance is demonstrated through applications in high-order stencilled WENO schemes and the approximation of periodic functions like $\sin(x)$. The study further highlights the technique's utility in generating unstructured grids with high-order compatible stencilles for solving systems with known analytic solutions or when employing adaptive mesh refinement.
